name: humanoid-hold
$comment: Humanoid torso with two stacked 7-DOF SRS arms (shoulder pitch-roll-yaw, elbow, forearm yaw, wrist pitch-roll, shoulder and wrist axis offsets) holding one box with both hands. Plant: spatial multibond chains (compliant Revolute3D joints, RigidBody3D links with illustrative masses), per joint a bond-graph drive (motor torque MSe, reflected rotor inertia I, elastic gear C/R with a torque sensor De, joint friction R), the box on two stiff grasp springs (Revolute3D welds with a torsion spring on the axis). Firmware at 1 kHz: ObjectTrajectory -> ArmIK per arm (damped least squares with a null-space pull toward home plus the elbow bias; J5 locked with Traj/dof6) -> ArmServo (PID). The ideal-SRS pair (IdealL/IdealR) is kinematic and drawn beside the robot.

plots.title: Hand pose errors (simulated vs grasp target)
IK solution errors and nearest limit

options.text: **Redundancy.** A rigid grasp fixes the full pose of each hand (3 position + 3 orientation), so two hands on one object give **12 constraints**. Two 7-DOF arms have **14 joints: 2 left over**, one self-motion per arm (the elbow swings about the shoulder-wrist line while the hand stays put). Two 6-DOF arms (J5 locked) have **12 joints for 12 constraints: no slack**, so the object pose fixes both postures, the elbow bias does nothing, and at the default pose the arms run into J3 and J6 limits and miss the grasp by about 3.5 mm and 3.3 deg. Here the arms are a multibody model on joint servos and the box hangs on two stiff grasp springs: what the IK cannot match becomes grasp load.
